home.headline: A free, bilingual platform for consumer behaviour research
home.lede: Build anything from a simple questionnaire to an interactive experiment, run it with participants in Arabic or English, and export clean data for analysis. No fees, no institutional licence, no code.

questionnaires.title: Questionnaires
questionnaires.body: Twelve question types, attention checks and reusable blocks, arranged in any order you choose.

experiments.title: Media experiments
experiments.body: Show images, video and audio with exposure control. Conditions, shopping environments and online shops are on the roadmap.

bilingual.title: Arabic and English
bilingual.body: Right-to-left and left-to-right done properly, for both researchers and participants.

export.title: Clean exports
export.body: One row per participant, a codebook with Arabic and English labels, and the exact study version used.

free.title: Free, always
free.body: No subscriptions, no paid tiers, no selling of participant data. Designed to be self-hosted by universities.

home.footer: A research tool, not a commercial product. Limits exist only to keep the free service stable and are explained in the documentation.

settings.languagesHint: With two languages, participants choose at the start.
settings.showProgress: Show a progress bar to participants
settings.allowResume: Let participants resume after an accidental refresh
settings.allowResumeHint: Uses a random token stored in the participant's browser. No personal data is stored.
settings.themeNote: Phase 1 uses the neutral research theme. More themes arrive with the interactive environments.
settings.usesDeceptionHint: E.g. an AI-generated advert that is not disclosed. You will be reminded to add a debrief.
settings.eventsNavigation: Navigation: when each page is shown and left, and when the tab is hidden
settings.eventsNavigationHint: Used for time per page and drop-off analysis.
settings.eventsMedia: Media exposure: visible time, plays, pauses, seeks and progress
settings.eventsMediaHint: Used for computed variables such as seconds an advert was visible or the percentage of a video watched.
settings.eventsNever: Never recorded: keystrokes, mouse movements, camera, microphone or location.
settings.eventsEnvironment: Shopping behaviour: walking past, stopping at and entering stores, product views, basket changes, choices
settings.eventsEnvironmentHint: Needed for the village's computed variables (entered, dwell time, products viewed).

share.notPublished: Publish the study to get a participant link.
share.paramsHint: Anything you add to the link, such as ?pid=ABC123 from a participant panel, is saved with the session.
share.testLink: Test link (only works while you are signed in)
share.testHint: Test sessions are flagged and left out of exports by default. Add &f_variable=value to force a factor level.
share.lockHint: Mark this version as locked, e.g. the version validated in a pilot. Published versions never change either way.
share.versionsHint: Published versions can never be edited. Publishing changes creates a new version; every session records the version it used.
share.deleteWarning: Deleting removes the study, all versions and all participant data permanently.
share.typeTitle: Type the study title to confirm: {title}
share.saveTemplateHint: Saves the last saved draft (blocks, design and settings) so you can start new studies from it in any of your projects. Participant data is never included.

media.openLibrary: Upload files in the media library

block.heading: Heading
block.consentHint: Use the consent text approved by your ethics committee. Participants must actively agree; declining ends the session politely. The exact text shown is stored with each consent record.
block.consentVersionHint: Change this whenever the consent text changes, e.g. 2 or 2026-10.
block.caption: Caption
block.plainTextHint: Plain text. Blank lines start new paragraphs.
block.requireVideoEnd: Participants must play videos and audio to the end
block.questions: {n, plural, =0 {No questions} one {# question} other {# questions}}
block.completionCodeHint: Shown to participants at the end, e.g. for a participant panel.
block.redirectUrlHint: Participants are sent here a few seconds after finishing. Must start with https://. You can insert '{code}', '{session}' or any link parameter such as '{PROLIFIC_PID}'.
block.blockIdHint: Stable identifier used in the data.
block.itemShowIfHint: E.g. show the AI-generated version only when this brand is the participant's target brand.
block.pipingHint: You can insert '{{stimulus}}' (current repetition) or '{{factor:variable}}' (an assigned level).
block.uniqueCode: Give each participant a unique completion code
block.uniqueCodeHint: Stored with the session and exported, so you can match panel submissions.
block.eligibleIfHint: Participants who do not meet this rule see the message below and the session ends. Their answers are kept and the session is marked as screened out.
block.debriefHint: Required when the study withholds or disguises information, such as an undisclosed AI-generated advert.
block.exclusionHint: Participants enter an identifier, such as their email address. Only a salted hash is kept, in a list private to your account; the identifier itself is never stored. Use it to stop people taking part in related studies twice.
block.recordListHint: Lower-case letters, numbers and dashes, e.g. foodcourt-2026. Leave empty to only check.

question.variableHint: Column name in the export. Keep it stable.
question.variableInvalid: Start with a letter; use only letters, numbers and _.
question.randomizeHint: Order is seeded per participant, so it can be reproduced.
question.attentionCheckHint: Participants who give a different answer are flagged in the export. They are not removed.

logic.valueHint: Use answer codes (e.g. 1), factor level values (e.g. A) or condition codes. Separate several values with commas.

display.title: Display & logic
display.showToHint: Leave all unticked to show the block to everyone.
display.noConditions: Add conditions in the Design tab to show blocks to specific groups.
display.showIfHint: Skip or branching logic, checked when the participant reaches this block.
display.repeatHint: E.g. ask the same scale once per brand. Variables get the level as a suffix (att_A, att_B…). Use '{{stimulus}}' in text to show the current level.
display.orderGroupHint: Blocks in the same group swap positions according to the group's method (Design tab).

design.conditionsHint: Each participant is assigned to one condition when they start. Show blocks to specific conditions in each block's Display & logic panel.
design.noConditions: No conditions: everyone sees the same study.
design.label: Label (only you see it)

balanced.title: Balanced (recommended)
balanced.body: Permuted blocks keep group sizes equal (or in proportion to the weights) at every point of data collection.

random.title: Simple random
random.body: Each participant is drawn independently. Group sizes can drift apart.

design.quotaHint: A quota counts completed, non-test sessions. Full conditions stop receiving participants; when all are full, the study stops accepting new ones.
design.orderGroupsHint: Counterbalance the order of whole blocks, e.g. two questionnaires shown in either order.
design.name: Name
design.members: {n, plural, =0 {No blocks yet: choose this group in a block's Display & logic panel.} one {# block} other {# blocks}}
design.factorsHint: Values assigned to each participant at the start and stored as their own columns, e.g. which brand gets the AI-generated advert, the order of adverts, or which offer goes to which store.
design.factorsUsage: Use factors in rules (Display & logic), to repeat blocks per level, in media item rules, and in text with '{{factor:variable}}'.

pick.title: Pick one
pick.body: Each participant gets one level, e.g. target_brand = B.

order.title: Order
order.body: Each participant gets all levels in an order, e.g. ad_order = C>A>B.

mapping.title: Mapping
mapping.body: Levels are matched one-to-one with targets, e.g. offers onto stores.

design.variableInvalid: Start with a letter; use only letters, numbers and _.

methodHints.balanced: Every level is used equally often (permuted blocks).
methodHints.fixed: Everyone gets the same value or order.
methodHints.latin: Each level appears in each position equally often, and each level follows every other equally often (Williams design).
methodHints.permutation: Cycles through every possible order (up to 6 levels).

design.refHint: Link levels to library items so blocks can use them, e.g. offers mapped onto stores, or the brand whose advert is AI-generated.

warnings.title: {n, plural, =0 {No design warnings} one {# design warning} other {# design warnings}}
warnings.hint: Warnings never block publishing. Dismissed warnings are recorded in the audit log.

no_consent.title: No consent block
no_consent.why: Participants must actively agree before taking part. Add a Consent block unless your ethics approval says otherwise.

detection_before_attitude.title: Detection question comes before attitude measures
detection_before_attitude.why: Asking whether something was AI-generated makes participants suspicious, which changes later attitude and trust answers.

deception_no_debrief.title: Deception without a debrief
deception_no_debrief.why: Studies that withhold or disguise information should end with a Debrief block explaining what happened and why.

no_attention_check.title: No attention check in a long questionnaire ({n} questions)
no_attention_check.why: Long questionnaires invite careless answering. Mark at least one instructed-response question as an attention check.

condition_imbalance.title: Conditions differ a lot in length
condition_imbalance.why: Condition {high} has many more blocks or questions than {low}. Differences in fatigue or time can be confused with the manipulation.

no_manipulation_check.title: No manipulation check
no_manipulation_check.why: With several conditions, add a questionnaire marked as a manipulation check to verify participants noticed the manipulation.

group_spans_consent.title: Order group crosses the consent block
group_spans_consent.why: Group {group} has blocks both before and after consent, so some participants could see study content before agreeing.

screening_after_content.title: Screening comes after study content
screening_after_content.why: Screen participants before showing stimuli or questions, so ineligible people do not see study material.

env.libraryHint: Stores, products, offers and ads come from your library.
env.heading: Heading
env.storesHint: Add as many as you like; around 12 or fewer keeps the street easy to explore on a phone.
env.orderFactorHint: An order factor whose levels are linked to these items (or their brands).

offerModes.fixed: Same offer for everyone (per store or product)
offerModes.factor: From a mapping factor (offers onto stores or products)

env.offerFactorHint: A mapping factor whose levels are linked to offers and whose targets are linked to these stores or products.
env.variablePrefixHint: Export columns start with this, e.g. {prefix}_S1_entered.

versionModes.targeted: One brand (from a factor) gets a different version

env.targetedHint: E.g. the participant's target_brand shows its "ai" version and every other brand shows "authentic".
env.disclosureHint: Label text, position and style are set on each ad in the library. Tick conditions to show it only to them (none ticked = everyone).
env.requireEnd: Videos must be played to the end
env.showProducts: Show a product and its price on each card
env.considerationHint: Yes/no, e.g. "Would you consider buying here?". Leave empty to skip.
env.productsHint: Products come from your library. Their order follows the product order setting; sponsored products are also lifted to the top of listings.
env.requireCheckout: Participants must go through checkout to finish
env.requireCheckoutHint: When off, a “Leave the shop” button lets participants finish without ordering.
env.shopPrefixHint: Export columns start with this, e.g. {prefix}_P1_qty.
env.feedPrefixHint: Export columns start with this, e.g. {prefix}_p1_liked.
env.platformName: Feed name shown at the top
env.feedPostsHint: Organic posts are written here. Sponsored posts show an ad from your library, with its version and disclosure rules. Like counts are stimuli you set, not real data.
env.postAuthorAd: Account name (leave empty to use the ad's name)
env.showCountsHint: The counts are the numbers you set on each post, plus one if the participant likes it.

data.title: Participants & data
data.statsNote: Counts use real recorded sessions only. Test sessions are counted separately.

export.nothing: Publish the study to collect data.
export.includeTestHint: Off by default so test data never mixes with real data.
export.note: Files are UTF-8 with Arabic intact. Put the SPSS syntax next to the data CSV and run it. In R use readr::read_csv(); in Python use pandas.read_csv(encoding="utf-8-sig").
export.events: Event log (CSV, one row per event)

data.noSessionsHint: Share the participant link or run a test session from the Share tab.
data.deleteTestConfirm: Delete all test sessions for this study?

media.title: Media library
media.subtitle: Images, video and audio for your studies. Files are private until a published study uses them. Maximum {mb} MB per file.

media.emptyHint: Upload images, videos or audio to use them in studies.

settings.typeEmail: Type your email address to confirm: {email}

library.title: Library
library.subtitle: Brands, stores, products, offers and adverts you can reuse across studies. Studies copy what they use when you publish, so editing the library never changes a running study.

emptyHint.brand: Brands give stores and adverts a name, colours and a logo. Mark fictional brands as fictional.
emptyHint.store: Stores appear in the shopping village and the store choice task.
emptyHint.product: Products are sold in stores. Prices use the currency you choose.
emptyHint.offer: Offers (e.g. 50% off, buy one get one free) are shown on stores and change the effective price.
emptyHint.ad: Adverts can have several versions, e.g. authentic and AI-generated.

about.brand: Select a brand to edit it, or create a new one.
about.store: Select a store to edit it, or create a new one. A store sells products and can show adverts on its front and inside.
about.product: Select a product to edit it, or create a new one.
about.offer: Select an offer to edit it, or create a new one. The effective unit price is calculated for you.
about.ad: Select an advert to edit it, or create a new one. Each version has its own image or video.

library.codeHint: Short, unique, used in exported column names (e.g. S1).
library.codeTaken: That code is already used. Choose another.
library.name: Name
library.snapshotNote: Published studies keep the version they were published with. Publish again to use your changes.
library.fictionalHint: Reminds you to say so in the debrief.
library.displayTextHint: What participants see on the store, e.g. "Buy 1 get 1 free".
library.effectiveExample: Example: a product at {base} costs {effective} per unit with this offer.
library.signTextHint: Leave empty to use the store name.
library.versionsHint: E.g. "authentic" and "ai". Studies choose which version each participant sees.
library.disclosureHint: Shown on this advert only when a study's rules say so (e.g. in the label condition).
library.ratingsNote: Written by you for the study. If they are fictional, say so in your debrief.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.notPublishedHint: Analytics appear once the study is published and people have taken part.
analytics.noDataHint: No one has started this study yet with the current filters. Test sessions are hidden unless you include them.
analytics.note: Computed from recorded sessions only. Questions and blocks follow the latest version (v{version}).
analytics.testWarning: Includes {n} test sessions. These are not real participants; do not report them.
analytics.lastDays: Showing the last {n} days with sessions.
analytics.funnelHint: Sessions that submitted each block. A drop between two rows shows where people left.
analytics.timeHint: Median seconds from entering to submitting a block (repeated blocks pooled).
analytics.envN: {n, plural, one {# participant finished this block} other {# participants finished this block}}
analytics.checkoutLine: {started} went to checkout, {done} of {n} placed the simulated order
analytics.multiNote: Participants could pick more than one answer, so percentages can add up to more than 100%.
analytics.textNote: Open text answers are in the CSV export.

templates.title: Templates
templates.subtitle: Start a new study from a ready-made template or from a study you saved. Each one creates a normal draft you can edit freely.
templates.needProject: Create a project first; new studies are added to a project.
templates.noSavedHint: Open any study, go to Share & versions, and use “Save as a template”.
templates.howToSave: To add one, open a study and use “Save as a template” under Share & versions. Templates use items from your library, which stay where they are.
